newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Greece says Turkey could be punished over Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Greece says Turkey could be punished over Cyprus.

text.p: Turkey must face sanctions if it continues to defy the international community over the occupied island of Cyprus, Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said on Friday.

"I can't see at all why what is applied in Iraq (sanctions) should not be applied to Turkey if they persist in defying the international community," Pangalos told a news conference during an official visit to Lisbon.
"There cannot be good offenders and bad offenders. We must have a system of rules and these rules should be applied to everyone," he added.

"We cannot consider any solution based on separation," Pangalos said, flanked by Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama. "These people (Cypriots) must have the right to live where they want, move where they want and do what they want to do.

"It is for the international community, the European Union, United States and United Nations to propose concrete steps and then if some of those involved in these questions do not abide by these proposals, sanctions should be imposed on them."
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops invaded the island in the wake of a short-lived coup engineered by the military regime ruling Greece.

Only Turkey recognises a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state set up in the north of the island in 1983, where some 30,000 mainland troops are stationed, and the protracted dispute remains a source of tension between Turkey and Greece, its neighbour and NATO partner.

Tension in Cyprus has risen considerably in the past month after the killings of two Greek Cypriots by security forces and civilians in the Turkish-occupied areas during demonstrations against the division of the island.
